'''Consuelo Martínez López''' (born 1955) is a Spanish mathematician, and a frequent collaborator of [[Fields Medal]]ist [[Efim Zelmanov]]. Her research topics include [[abstract algebra]] including [[group theory]] and [[superalgebra]]s, [[algebraic coding theory]], and [[cryptography]]. She is the professor of algebra at the [[University of Oviedo]].{{r|icmat}}

==Education and career==
Martínez was born in 1955 in [[Ferrol, Spain]], the daughter of a teacher. She earned a [[Licentiate (degree)|licenciate]] in mathematics in 1977 from the [[University of Zaragoza]],{{r|icmat}} and completed her Ph.D. at the University of Zaragoza in 1980. Her dissertation, ''Formaciones saturadas en una clase de grupos localmente finitos PI-resolubles'', concerned [[group theory]], and was supervised by Javier Otal.{{r|mg}} She became professor of algebra at the University of Oviedo in 2005.{{r|pjp}}

As well as her research and teaching in mathematics, Martínez has participated in joint work of the [[Royal Spanish Academy]] and [[Royal Spanish Mathematical Society]] to include mathematical terminology in the ''[[Diccionario de la lengua española]]''.{{r|dict}}

==Recognition==
In 2018, Martínez won both the medal of the [[Royal Spanish Mathematical Society]],{{r|lne}} and the Julio Peláez Prize for women in the sciences, given by the Tatiana Pérez de Guzmán el Bueno Foundation.{{r|pjp}}

She was elected as a corresponding member of the [[Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences]] in 2021.{{r|rac}}
